title: quant: INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant-fusion kernels + scheduler/tuning for kvcache/batching
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: reduce token-level latency and cost for quantized inference paths by combining dequant fusion, SmoothQuant-aware kernel selection, and scheduler-level tuning for KV cache hotspots and continuous batching. This PR implements optimized INT8/FP8 codepaths that fuse dequantization with successive GEMM kernels where possible, introduces a SmoothQuant-aware weight layout and scaling pass, and adds scheduler heuristics to prioritize KV cache hot-shard affinity and continuous-batching friendly packing.

What changed (high level):
- New fused kernels: quant_dequant_gemm_{int8,fp8}_fused (C++/CUDA) with AVX/AMX and CUDA tensor core fallbacks. These accept per-channel SmoothQuant scales and emit fused outputs without a separate dequant stage.
- SmoothQuant preprocessing: runtime weight-layout selector and a lightweight scaling metadata table to avoid per-inference re-layout.
- Scheduler changes: affinity hinting for KV cache hot keys, preferential packing for short-tail sequences to improve continuous batching without increasing tail latency, and a backpressure tweak to avoid head-of-line blocking when fused kernels are in use.
- KV cache micro-optimizations: lazy materialization for dequantized cache entries when downstream kernels can consume quantized inputs, reducing memory traffic.
- Tests and benchmarks: microbenchmarks for 1536/2048/4096 context lengths across a set of representative open models; end-to-end perf harness runs; integration tests for correctness against float32 reference.

Implementation notes:
- Kernel files are under src/runtime/kernels/quant/ and use a shared utility for per-channel scale application. Fallbacks remain in-place: when upstream quant metadata is missing we fall back to the previous dequant + GEMM path.
- Scheduler heuristics are opt-in behind a runtime flag (RUNTIME_QUANT_SCHEDULER=1) to allow safe rollout.
- We added runtime feature flags and an API to expose kernel capability strings for selection and debugging.

Benchmarks:
- On NVIDIA A100, 4k context, batch=1: ~18% p99 token latency reduction for INT8 fused path vs previous int8 dequant-then-gemm.
- On AMD MI250, medium sequence lengths, FP8 fused path shows ~12% average latency improvement and ~15% throughput improvement in sustained streaming workloads.
- End-to-end 95th latency for short-tail interactive workload improved by 10-14% due to scheduler packing improvements.

Compatibility and safety:
- All new kernel paths include a float32 shadow check in CI for accuracy regressions. We run delta-checks against a float32 reference on a fixed eval set; differences are within expected rounding error for INT8/FP8 with SmoothQuant.
- No API surface change for customers. The scheduler heuristics are disabled by default in the hosted tier until we finish Canary and Dedicated rollout testing.

Checklist: 
- [x] Unit tests for new kernels (CPU + CUDA smoke)
- [x] Integration tests for KV cache correctness with quantized entries
- [x] Performance microbench harness and baseline comparisons
- [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan in release notes
- [x] Documentation snippets added to runtime/README about flags and kernel capability strings

Related: ENG-2123 (quant kernel perf initiative), ENG-2150 (continuous batching improvements). This PR consolidates several experimental branches and is intended as the initial rollout for the quant fusion work.

Notes on CI history: initial runs failed a CUDA flakiness test (cuda_kernels_smoke) on the MI250 lane; I pushed a small reorder fix and retriggered CI. All required checks are green on merge.
